findings.reason: the node's declared write scope names a symbol it cannot resolve, and §1's evidence trace for the double read cannot be checked as written.
findings.text: `_read_new` is named as a write target in `imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py` and cited in §1 as the second reader of the consumed prefix, but no symbol of that name exists anywhere in `imas_ambix/` or `tests/`; the generator that performs both reads is `_resume` (`telemetry_index.py:1341`), and the `head = handle.read(start)` §1 quotes sits inside it at line 1404

findings.reason: as written the measure fails once an hour by construction, so a coordinator reads a non-defect as a failed deployment or a worker removes the hourly verification the negative controls depend on to make the number pass.
findings.text: the post-deployment acceptance "the ingest pid's `read_bytes` advances by at most 100 MB over 300 s" is contradicted by the section's own mechanism, which re-verifies each source's whole consumed prefix once per `FULL_IDENTITY_INTERVAL` (3,600 s), and the live sources §1 measures are ~1.31 GB, so one 300 s window in every hour carries a ~1.3 GB read

findings.reason: a node that edits the single named writer leaves two of the six script kinds, including the log the runtime-check reader at `cli.py:4478` resolves, still writing to the submitting directory, and fails its own done-when.
findings.text: "the change is made at the single `#SBATCH --output=` writer in `slurm.py`" is not true of the scripts the section's own done-when names: `cli.py:3782` (runtime-check, `ambix-runtime-check-<engine>-%j.log`) and `cli.py:4258` (setup, `ambix-setup-<engine>-%j.log`) emit their own literal directives inside `cli.py` and never reach `slurm.py:150`

findings.reason: this is the plan's only irreversible deletion of existing files, and without a control the node can neither show its guard refuses nor show the step did its work.
findings.text: the archive step "removes an original only after its archive decompresses to the same SHA-256", but no done-when bullet requires showing that a mismatching archive leaves the original in place; "the archive step's printed list accounts for all 451 files, with no SHA mismatch" is satisfied by an archive step that compresses and never removes anything

findings.reason: §9 is declared `deferred` and is not dispatched, so nothing consumes the edge.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` declares `{s5:[s3,s4], s6:[s4,s5], s7:[s6]}`, so §9 carries no edge to §8 although §9's text ("deferred until §8's breakdown says how much the pruning would recover") makes §8 its gate

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — `_read_new` (§1 line 40, §3 line 106) resolves nowhere in `imas_ambix/` or `tests/`; every other anchor checked resolves: `watch.py:91` is `DEFAULT_INDEX_PATH` with exactly two `Path(index_path or DEFAULT_INDEX_PATH)` fallbacks (1306, 1433) and three `--index` help strings in `cli.py` (3092, 3193, 3288), `_was_rewritten` (1421) and `_digest_of` (1804) exist, `UNIQUE (host, boot_id, inode, offset)` is at `telemetry_index.py:266` as §4 assumes, `watch_publish.one_iteration` is at `watch_publish.py:124`, `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py` exists, the guard test `tests/test_agent_serve_registry.py::test_agent_package_modules_parse_with_serving_python` exists, `docs/figures/watch-index-lifecycle/data-flow.svg` exists, and `serving-record-warehouse` §21, §24 and followup `f-srw-020` all resolve with the content the plan attributes to them.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §3, §4, §5 and §6 each name a control that can fail, and §3's three rewrite cases are stated with the time they must be detected at, but §7's delete-after-verify step asks for no demonstration that a mismatching archive leaves its original in place.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gates land under the repository (§3's guard and ruff gate, §8's `docs/research/watch-index-size-and-retention.html` and its figure) or in the section's own "recorded here" bullet, and the durable artefacts §4 and §7 create go to GPFS under `~/.local/state/ambix/`; no gate writes to a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, ticket number or version tag enters a symbol, filename or comment; `FULL_IDENTITY_INTERVAL`, `index_placement.py` and the `-pre-rollup` snapshot suffix all name the mechanism, and `f-srw-020` appears only in plan prose in the plan that inherits it.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §1's root cause is supported by the cited code (verified: `time_weighted_mean` filters only `ts_epoch IS NOT NULL` and windows over every row, `telemetry_index.py:1559`), and §5's rollup mechanism can produce its done-when, but §3's stated mechanism cannot satisfy §3's own post-deployment measure.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of §3–§8 carries one deliverable, and §7's forward change and its one-off archive of the existing logs are two arms of the single "job logs leave the repository root" goal rather than two goals.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the declared edges s5→{s3,s4}, s6→{s4,s5} and s7→{s6} each resolve to a node that exists and match the ordering the followup states, but `plan-section-depends-on` carries no `s9` entry although §9's own text makes it wait on §8.
